title: Finite-clopen detection of constructibility and fixed cohomological and Tor bounds
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-pur-conventions].

Put $A=A_{E,n}$ for $n\ge1$ and let $r_i$ be derived restriction on $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-tensor]. A sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules is constructible in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] if and only if every $F|_{X_i}$ is constructible. More precisely, restriction of a finite locally closed constructibility stratification intersects its strata with $X_i$; conversely the component strata, viewed as subschemes of $X$, form a finite constructibility stratification with the same locally constant finite-module models.

For any $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and any integers $a\le b$, its cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$ if and only if the cohomology of every $r_iK$ does. The cohomology sheaves of $K$ are constructible if and only if those of every $r_iK$ are. Tor amplitude in the fixed interval $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] is equivalent to Tor amplitude in that same interval on every component: the test objects are all module sheaves in degree zero, including those obtained by zero insertion from a single component.

Consequently the unbounded restriction equivalence restricts to equivalences on $D^b_c(-,A)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Any common cohomological bounds, and any common Tor bounds, for the finitely many component complexes are bounds for the glued complex. Empty components and $I=\varnothing$ are allowed, and the zero object satisfies every such interval condition.

proof.text: Identify actual ordinary inverse image with sectionwise clopen restriction followed by the coefficient equivalence. Use uniqueness of the ring-sheaf and module left adjoints, the canonical constant-ring comparison, and restriction of scalars along the resulting ring isomorphisms. Compose the proved moduleGluing equivalence with these coefficient equivalences. Its actual functor is the tuple of ordinary pullbacks. Apply the proved derivedPi_isEquivalence to these exact functors and their quasi-inverse, obtaining the tuple of actual derived pullbacks.

proof.text: The module equivalence detects zero objects. Exact pullback commutes with each homology functor, so homology vanishing and constructible cohomology are detected componentwise. The global cohomological support is the union of the component supports. Subsets of a common interval are detected on that union; finite support is equivalent to finite support on each member of a finite family.

source.place: def-pur-section-invariant, final invertibility assertion: agent finite-clopen constructibility and fixed-interval Tor argument, old item step 8; definitions def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility and def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude.

proof.text: Use the native ringed derived tensor and its K-flat representative isomorphism to express the published Tor-amplitude predicate as vanishing of tensor with every degree-zero module. The canonical tensor pullback comparison identifies restriction of each such tensor with the local tensor. Zero detection proves the global bound from the component bounds. Conversely, insert an arbitrary module on one component and zero on every other component, apply the module equivalence inverse, and use its counit to identify the chosen component. This gives every local test module without a separate product-bounds theorem.

proof.text: Bounded constructibility is finite homological support together with constructibility in every degree, hence is detected componentwise. For finite Tor amplitude, finitely many component lower and upper bounds have a lower bound a and upper bound b. Enlarge to [min(a,b),b] to handle even an empty index type, and use interval monotonicity. Restrict the actual derived equivalence to the two full subcategories, using their invariance under isomorphism. This construction retains the displayed forgetful-functor comparisons. Finally, a zero object has zero homology, and its derived tensor with any module is zero, giving every ordered interval.
